idiom_name: data class record + Exposed table with a coroutine Channel writer
implementation_notes: Kotlin adds two things to the JVM realization: an immutable data class as the stored record (a sealed hierarchy when payload shapes vary) and coroutines for the off-path copy - the tap becomes a Channel<MessageRecord> drained by a single writer coroutine on Dispatchers.IO, so the request path only offers and never touches the store, which is what replaces the classic Store object and interceptor. Persistence is a typed table: Exposed's Table/insert or SQLDelight's compile-time generated queries over the JDBC driver, both giving parameterised statements and transactions; on a Spring stack the JVM MessageStore remains available. Retention is a scheduled delete by timestamp, and reporting reads through Flow-based queries. The explicit abstraction is still worth writing when several stores must be behind one interface; otherwise the data class plus the channel is the pattern.
pitfalls: Channel.trySend drops silently when the buffer is full: recording the drop (counter, log, alert) is the difference between a monitored audit gap and a mystery.
Dispatchers.IO is a shared elastic pool; a writer loop that never yields to other work can starve it, so bound the writer's concurrency and keep the transaction block synchronous.
Suspending inside a JDBC transaction block moves the connection between threads mid-transaction; keep Exposed/SQLDelight transactions synchronous and confine them to the writer coroutine.
A data class whose toString includes the payload leaks audit content into application logs; exclude the payload or store its redacted form only.
